"""Polynomial-time reduction from 3-SAT (ThreeSat) to Exact Cover (ExactCover).

Construction
------------
Elements:
  * one element v_i per variable i (1..m),
  * one auxiliary element e_{j,k} for each literal occurrence k of clause j,
  * one element c_j per clause j.

Sets:
  * For each variable i, two sets
        T_i = {v_i} union {e_{j,k} : clause j has literal  x_i at position k}
        F_i = {v_i} union {e_{j,k} : clause j has literal -x_i at position k}
    Exactly one of them is picked, fixing the truth value of x_i.
  * For each clause j with occurrences e_{j,1},e_{j,2},e_{j,3} and element c_j,
    the seven gadget sets
        {c_j}, {c_j,e1}, {c_j,e2}, {c_j,e3},
        {c_j,e1,e2}, {c_j,e1,e3}, {c_j,e2,e3}.
    The gadget can cover c_j together with the auxiliaries of any subset of
    at most two literals, but NOT all three.  A gadget set may only use
    auxiliaries that the variable sets did not already cover, i.e. literals
    that are false.  Hence an exact cover exists iff every clause has at
    least one true literal.

The construction is linear in the size of the input.
"""

from __future__ import annotations


def reduce(instance):
    m = instance["num_vars"]
    clauses = instance["clauses"]
    n = len(clauses)

    nxt = 0
    var_elem = list(range(nxt, nxt + m))
    nxt += m

    # aux[j][k] : auxiliary element of the k-th literal of clause j
    aux = []
    for _ in range(n):
        row = list(range(nxt, nxt + 3))
        nxt += 3
        aux.append(row)

    clause_elem = list(range(nxt, nxt + n))
    nxt += n
    universe_size = nxt

    sets = []

    # Variable sets.
    for i in range(m):
        var = i + 1
        pos = [aux[j][k] for j in range(n) for k in range(3) if clauses[j][k] == var]
        neg = [aux[j][k] for j in range(n) for k in range(3) if clauses[j][k] == -var]
        sets.append([var_elem[i]] + pos)
        sets.append([var_elem[i]] + neg)

    # Clause gadgets.
    for j in range(n):
        c = clause_elem[j]
        e = aux[j]
        sets.append([c])
        for k in range(3):
            sets.append([c, e[k]])
        for k in range(3):
            for l in range(k + 1, 3):
                sets.append([c, e[k], e[l]])

    return {"universe_size": universe_size, "sets": sets}
EOF

"""Brute-force solvers for ThreeSat and ExactCover, written from the docstrings."""

from __future__ import annotations


def solve_three_sat(instance):
    m = instance["num_vars"]
    clauses = instance["clauses"]
    for mask in range(1 << m):
        ok = True
        for clause in clauses:
            sat = False
            for lit in clause:
                v = abs(lit)
                val = (mask >> (v - 1)) & 1
                if (lit > 0 and val == 1) or (lit < 0 and val == 0):
                    sat = True
                    break
            if not sat:
                ok = False
                break
        if ok:
            return True
    return False


def solve_exact_cover(instance):
    u = instance["universe_size"]
    sets = instance["sets"]
    # keep only non-empty, de-duplicated sets
    uniq = []
    seen = set()
    for s in sets:
        key = frozenset(s)
        if not key:
            continue
        if key in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(key)
        uniq.append(key)
    # membership: element -> list of set indices containing it
    cover = [[] for _ in range(u)]
    for idx, s in enumerate(uniq):
        for e in s:
            cover[e].append(idx)

    full = (1 << u) - 1

    def rec(covered):
        if covered == full:
            return True
        # pick an uncovered element with fewest candidate sets
        best = -1
        best_list = None
        rem = full & ~covered
        while rem:
            e = (rem & -rem).bit_length() - 1
            rem &= rem - 1
            cand = [idx for idx in cover[e] if not (uniq[idx] & covered)]
            if not cand:
                return False
            if best_list is None or len(cand) < len(best_list):
                best_list = cand
                best = e
                if len(cand) == 1:
                    break
        for idx in best_list:
            s = uniq[idx]
            if s & covered:
                continue
            if rec(covered | s):
                return True
        return False

    return rec(0)
EOF

"""Polynomial-time reduction from 3-SAT (ThreeSat) to Exact Cover (ExactCover).

Construction
------------
Elements:
  * one element v_i per variable i (1..m),
  * one auxiliary element e_{j,k} for each literal occurrence k of clause j,
  * one element c_j per clause j.

Sets:
  * For each variable i, two sets
        T_i = {v_i} union {e_{j,k} : clause j has literal  x_i at position k}
        F_i = {v_i} union {e_{j,k} : clause j has literal -x_i at position k}
    Exactly one of them is picked, fixing the truth value of x_i.
  * For each clause j with occurrences e_{j,1},e_{j,2},e_{j,3} and element c_j,
    the seven gadget sets
        {c_j}, {c_j,e1}, {c_j,e2}, {c_j,e3},
        {c_j,e1,e2}, {c_j,e1,e3}, {c_j,e2,e3}.
    The gadget can cover c_j together with the auxiliaries of any subset of
    at most two literals, but NOT all three.  A gadget set may only use
    auxiliaries that the variable sets did not already cover, i.e. literals
    that are false.  Hence an exact cover exists iff every clause has at
    least one true literal.

The construction is linear in the size of the input.
"""

from __future__ import annotations


def reduce(instance):
    m = instance["num_vars"]
    clauses = instance["clauses"]
    n = len(clauses)

    nxt = 0
    var_elem = list(range(nxt, nxt + m))
    nxt += m

    # aux[j][k] : auxiliary element of the k-th literal of clause j
    aux = []
    for _ in range(n):
        row = list(range(nxt, nxt + 3))
        nxt += 3
        aux.append(row)

    clause_elem = list(range(nxt, nxt + n))
    nxt += n
    universe_size = nxt

    sets = []

    # Variable sets.
    for i in range(m):
        var = i + 1
        pos = [aux[j][k] for j in range(n) for k in range(3) if clauses[j][k] == var]
        neg = [aux[j][k] for j in range(n) for k in range(3) if clauses[j][k] == -var]
        sets.append([var_elem[i]] + pos)
        sets.append([var_elem[i]] + neg)

    # Clause gadgets.
    for j in range(n):
        c = clause_elem[j]
        e = aux[j]
        sets.append([c])
        for k in range(3):
            sets.append([c, e[k]])
        for k in range(3):
            for l in range(k + 1, 3):
                sets.append([c, e[k], e[l]])

    return {"universe_size": universe_size, "sets": sets}
EOF

"""Brute-force solvers for ThreeSat and ExactCover, written from the docstrings."""

from __future__ import annotations


def solve_three_sat(instance):
    m = instance["num_vars"]
    clauses = instance["clauses"]
    for mask in range(1 << m):
        ok = True
        for clause in clauses:
            sat = False
            for lit in clause:
                v = abs(lit)
                val = (mask >> (v - 1)) & 1
                if (lit > 0 and val == 1) or (lit < 0 and val == 0):
                    sat = True
                    break
            if not sat:
                ok = False
                break
        if ok:
            return True
    return False


def solve_exact_cover(instance):
    u = instance["universe_size"]
    sets = instance["sets"]
    # keep only non-empty, de-duplicated sets
    uniq = []
    seen = set()
    for s in sets:
        key = frozenset(s)
        if not key:
            continue
        if key in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(key)
        uniq.append(key)
    # membership: element -> list of set indices containing it
    cover = [[] for _ in range(u)]
    for idx, s in enumerate(uniq):
        for e in s:
            cover[e].append(idx)

    full = (1 << u) - 1

    def rec(covered):
        if covered == full:
            return True
        # pick an uncovered element with fewest candidate sets
        best = -1
        best_list = None
        rem = full & ~covered
        while rem:
            e = (rem & -rem).bit_length() - 1
            rem &= rem - 1
            cand = [idx for idx in cover[e] if not (uniq[idx] & covered)]
            if not cand:
                return False
            if best_list is None or len(cand) < len(best_list):
                best_list = cand
                best = e
                if len(cand) == 1:
                    break
        for idx in best_list:
            s = uniq[idx]
            if s & covered:
                continue
            if rec(covered | s):
                return True
        return False

    return rec(0)
EOF

import random
import itertools
from problems import ThreeSat, ExactCover
from reduce import reduce
from solvers import solve_three_sat, solve_exact_cover

tests_run = 0
tests_passed = 0


def check(instance):
    global tests_run, tests_passed
    tests_run += 1
    ThreeSat.validate(instance)
    red = reduce(instance)
    ExactCover.validate(red)
    a = solve_three_sat(instance)
    b = solve_exact_cover(red)
    assert a == b, f"MISMATCH src={instance} src_ans={a} red={red} red_ans={b}"
    tests_passed += 1


def random_instance(m, n, rng):
    clauses = []
    for _ in range(n):
        vs = rng.sample(range(1, m + 1), 3)
        clause = [v if rng.random() < 0.5 else -v for v in vs]
        clauses.append(clause)
    return {"num_vars": m, "clauses": clauses}


def main():
    rng = random.Random(12345)

    # edge cases: no clauses, m = 0
    check({"num_vars": 0, "clauses": []})
    check({"num_vars": 1, "clauses": []})
    check({"num_vars": 5, "clauses": []})

    # exhaustive-ish small random tests
    for m in range(3, 8):
        for n in range(0, 8):
            for _ in range(40):
                check(random_instance(m, n, rng))

    # include duplicate clauses and unused variables
    for _ in range(200):
        m = rng.randint(3, 7)
        n = rng.randint(1, 6)
        inst = random_instance(m, n, rng)
        if n >= 1:
            inst["clauses"].append(list(inst["clauses"][0]))
        check(inst)

    # exhaustive over all 3-clauses for small m
    for m in (3, 4):
        all_clauses = []
        for vs in itertools.combinations(range(1, m + 1), 3):
            for signs in itertools.product((1, -1), repeat=3):
                all_clauses.append([s * v for s, v in zip(signs, vs)])
        for _ in range(300):
            n = rng.randint(0, 5)
            clauses = [list(rng.choice(all_clauses)) for _ in range(n)]
            check({"num_vars": m, "clauses": clauses})

    # known satisfiable / unsatisfiable
    check({"num_vars": 3, "clauses": [[1, 2, 3], [-1, -2, -3], [1, -2, 3], [-1, 2, -3]]})
    # all 8 clauses over 3 vars is unsat
    all8 = []
    for signs in itertools.product((1, -1), repeat=3):
        all8.append([s * v for s, v in zip(signs, (1, 2, 3))])
    check({"num_vars": 3, "clauses": all8})

    print(f"tests_run={tests_run} tests_passed={tests_passed}")
    assert tests_run == tests_passed


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

from solvers import solve_three_sat, solve_exact_cover

tests_run = 0
tests_passed = 0

    tests_run += 1
    ThreeSat.validate(instance)
    red = reduce(instance)
    ExactCover.validate(red)
    a = solve_three_sat(instance)
    b = solve_exact_cover(red)
    assert a == b, f"MISMATCH src={instance} src_ans={a} red={red} red_ans={b}"
    tests_passed += 1


def random_instance(m, n, rng):
    clauses = []
    for _ in range(n):
        vs = rng.sample(range(1, m + 1), 3)
        clause = [v if rng.random() < 0.5 else -v for v in vs]
        clauses.append(clause)
    return {"num_vars": m, "clauses": clauses}


def main():
    rng = random.Random(12345)

    # edge cases: no clauses, m = 0
    check({"num_vars": 0, "clauses": []})
    check({"num_vars": 1, "clauses": []})
    check({"num_vars": 5, "clauses": []})

    for m in range(3, 8):

    check({"num_vars": 3, "clauses": [[1, 2, 3], [-1, -2, -3], [1, -2, 3], [-1, 2, -3]]})
